questions: When adding business days to a date, which days count as non-working: only Saturday and Sunday, or are other days off too (for example a different weekend, or Friday/Saturday)?
When adding business days, should company or public holidays be skipped? If so, which holidays, and who maintains the list (it varies by year and region)?

When the starting date itself falls on a weekend or holiday, should counting begin from the next working day, or from the date as given? For example, does 5 business days from a Saturday land on the following Friday or the Monday after?
When the number of business days to add is zero, should the result be the start date itself even if it is a weekend or holiday, or should it move to the next working day?
Can the number of business days be negative (counting backwards)? If so, should it be supported, and does it follow the same weekend and holiday rules, or should it be rejected?
When the start date is blank, missing, impossible (such as 2026-0230), or not in YYYY-MM-DD form (such as 03/15/2026), should we reject it with an error, return a blank, or try to interpret it?
When the number of business days is missing, blank, fractional (like 2.5), or not a number, should it be rejected, rounded, or treated as zero?
Which month does the company's fiscal year start in (for example January, April, July, October)?
Is the fiscal year named after the calendar year in which it starts or the one in which it ends? For example, if the year starts in October 2026, is 2026-11-01 in FY2026 or FY2027?
Are fiscal quarters simply three-month blocks counted from the fiscal year start, or does the company use a different calendar, such as 4-4-5 weeks or quarters ending on particular weekdays?
What exact format should the fiscal label take (for example 'FY2026-Q3', 'FY26 Q3', '2026Q3'), and should the year be two or four digits?
When the date is blank, missing, impossible, or not in YYYY-MM-DD form, should the label be an error, blank, or something else?
Should a date far in the past or future (for example before 1900 or after 2100) be accepted, or rejected as probably a mistake?
What are the score cut-offs for each letter grade (for example A at 90 and above, B at 80, and so on)? Please give the lowest score for each letter.
Does the grading scale include plus and minus grades (A-, B+, etc.)? If so, what are their cut-offs?
Which letters exist at the bottom of the scale: is the lowest grade F, or is there also an E or a separate fail label? Below what score is it a fail?
If a score has decimals (like 89.5), should it be rounded to a whole number before grading (and with which rounding rule, e.g. half up), or compared exactly so 89.5 is still a B?
When a score is below 0 or above 100 (for example -5 or 105), should it be rejected as an error, clamped to 0 or 100, or given a grade anyway?
When the score is blank, missing, or not a number (for example 'absent' or 'N/A'), should we return an error, a blank, or a special grade such as 'Incomplete'?
Is there a grace period before a late fee applies? For example, is an invoice 1 to 5 days overdue free of any fee, and exactly how many days are free?
How is the late fee calculated: a flat amount, a percentage of the unpaid balance, a percentage per day or per month overdue, or a mix? Please give the rates and amounts.

Does the fee change with how late the invoice is, for example one rate for 1 to 30 days, a higher one for 31 to 60, and another beyond that? Please give the day ranges and the rate for each, and say whether a boundary day such as day 30 belongs to the lower or higher band.
Is there a minimum late fee (for example never less than 500 cents) when a fee applies, even on a very small balance?
Is there a maximum late fee, either a fixed amount or a percentage of the balance, that the fee can never exceed?
When the fee is a percentage and the result is not a whole number of cents, should it round to the nearest cent, always up, or always down?
Should the late fee be zero when the unpaid balance is zero, and what should happen when the balance is negative (a credit)? Return zero, or an error?
When the overdue days are zero or negative (the invoice is not yet due), should the fee be zero or should the input be rejected?
When the balance or number of days overdue is blank, missing, fractional, or not a number, should we reject it, treat it as zero, or round it?
What are the loyalty tier names and their requirements? For each tier (for example Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum), what are the minimum points and the minimum years of membership?

To reach a tier, must a customer meet both the points and the years requirement, or does either one suffice? For example, does someone with 10,000 points but only 1 year of membership get the high tier?
Is a customer exactly at a threshold (for example exactly 1,000 points) in the higher tier or the lower tier?
What tier name should customers below the lowest threshold get: a base tier such as 'Basic', a blank, or no tier?
How are years of membership counted: whole completed years only, or can fractional years count (for example 1.5)? If a customer has 0.9 years, do they count as 0 or 1 year?
When the points balance is negative, blank, missing, or not a whole number, should we reject it, treat it as zero, or round it? And the same for years of membership.
Is there a top level where points above a certain number make no further difference, or can the tier be capped for any reason, such as a customer account that is suspended?
How many digits at the end of the account number should stay visible: the last 4, or a different number?
Which character should replace the hidden digits (for example '*', 'X', or '•')?
Should the mask keep the original length of the account number, with one masking character for each hidden digit, or use a fixed number of masking characters?
Should dashes, spaces, or other separators in the account number be kept in place, removed, or masked too? For example, how should '1234-5678-9012' be shown?
When the account number is shorter than or equal to the number of visible digits (for example only 3 characters), should it be shown in full, fully masked, or rejected as an error?
When the account number is blank or missing, should we return a blank, a fully masked placeholder, or an error?
Can account numbers contain letters (for example IBAN-style numbers), and should those be masked the same way as digits?
Should leading and trailing spaces around the account number be stripped before masking?
What is the total fixed width of the formatted code (for example 6 or 8 characters)? Is it the same everywhere, or does it vary by system?
When the code is longer than the fixed width (for example a 9-digit number in an 8-character field), should it be rejected as an error, cut to fit, or shown in full? If it is cut, from which end?
When the code is negative, how should the sign be shown (for example '-00042' or a leading minus within the width), or should negative codes be rejected?
When the code has decimals (like 42.7), should it be rounded to a whole number (and how), cut off, or rejected?
When the code is blank, missing, or not a number (for example 'ABC'), should we return an error, blank, or all zeros?
Should padding be on the left with zeros only, or do some legacy systems need a different padding character or padding on the right?

How is shipping priced by weight: a table of weight bands for each zone (for example 0 to 500 g, 501 g to 1,000 g, and so on), a base price plus an amount per extra kilogram, or something else? Please give the prices for each zone.
For each weight band, does a parcel exactly on the upper limit (for example exactly 500 g) fall into the lower band or the next one?
Should weight be rounded up to the next full unit (such as the next 100 g or 500 g, or the next kilogram) before pricing? If so, which unit?
Is there a minimum shipping charge, even for a very light parcel?
What is the heaviest parcel we ship? When a parcel is over that limit, should we reject it, or charge a special rate (and what rate)?
Which zone numbers are valid (for example 1 to 5)? What should happen with a zone that doesn't exist, such as 0, 9, or a negative number: reject it or use a default zone?

When the weight is zero, negative, blank, missing, or fractional, should the charge be rejected, zero, or the minimum charge? And should a fractional weight be rounded up, down, or to the nearest gram?
When the zone is blank, missing, or not a whole number, should it be rejected or defaulted to a particular zone?
Are there any surcharges or discounts that apply to the shipping charge (fuel surcharge, remote area, free shipping above a certain weight or order value) that the function must include?

When a bill is split evenly and the total doesn't divide into whole cents, who pays the extra cents? For example, 1,000 cents among 3 people is 333.33 each: does everyone pay 334 (rounded up), 333 (rounded down), or do one or two people pay a cent more?
Should the amount each person pays be rounded up, down, or to the nearest cent, if the function returns a single per-person figure?
The tip is already included in the bill amount. Does anything else need to be done with the tip, such as adding a service charge, or is it simply part of the total being divided?
What is the maximum number of people the bill may be split between? Is there a limit?
When the number of people is zero, negative, blank, missing, or fractional (like 2.5), should we reject it, treat it as one person, or round it?
When the bill total is zero, negative, blank, missing, or not a whole number of cents, should it be rejected, treated as zero, or rounded?

Which value should be treated as the middle when the group has an even number of orders, for example 4 orders of 10, 20, 30, 40: the average of the two middle values (25), the lower one (20), or the higher one (30)?
If the average of the two middle values isn't a whole number of cents (for example 10 and 15 gives 12.5), should it round up, down, or to the nearest cent, and which way at exactly half?
What counts as a missing amount to be ignored: blank, null, the word 'N/A', or also zero? Should an order of exactly zero be counted or ignored?
Should negative order amounts (refunds or credits) be included in the middle value, ignored, or rejected?
When the group is empty, or every amount is missing, should the result be zero, blank, or an error?
When an order amount isn't a number (for example text like 'abc'), should it be ignored like a missing amount or should the whole calculation be rejected?
Should cancelled, test, or unpaid orders be excluded from the middle value, or does every order in the group count?
